SMBP · B2B Personal Finance · Screen ↔ Step ↔ Backend contract

Screen reference: map + calculation lab

Every screen in Gấu trắng's prototype mapped to its user-story step, the backend behaviour it triggers, and the market-practice check. Thumbnails are live captures from the prototype. This is the handoff contract for Hailey's backend feature creation — build from the US column, not the prototype, wherever they disagree (§06).

06

Decisions needed before Hailey builds

Where prototype and US disagree, the US wins by default — but each needs an explicit call so the prototype gets corrected, not silently ignored.
Conflict · Gấu trắng to confirm1 · Manual "Buyout details" screen vs AECB auto-fill

Prototype asks the customer to type outstanding balance / EMI / months left. US pulls everything from AECB. Recommendation: kill the manual screen — bureau data is the single source, matching the liability letter.

Conflict · Gấu trắng to confirm2 · Processing-fee card payment vs deduct-from-finance

Prototype has a 3-D Secure payment screen; AMP-3404 AC9 says B2B collects no payment — fees deduct at disbursal. Recommendation: no PSP in B2B scope; mark the screen B2C-only.

Watch · decide once3 · One signature model

Swipe-stamp (T&C/KFS), drawn signature (prototype), EFR signature + OTP (cheque). Pick the evidence model per document class before AMP-3757 is built.

Watch · config not copy4 · Numbers that must come from config

Min income (prototype "7,000"), re-apply block ("90 days"), grace range, liability-letter validity (default 15), fee lines in KFS. None may be hardcoded from prototype copy.

Watch · scope check5 · Manual document-upload eKYC route

Prototype offers upload-instead-of-scan; no AC covers it. Include only if the bank accepts assisted-KYC risk; otherwise drop.

Carry-over6 · Known spec gaps still open

G4 standing check for Buyout · settlement-execution (manager's cheque) workflow · cooling-off AC12 behaviours · BP-vs-DP gate defaults (G2/G3) · shortfall check trigger point (AMP-3732 AC6 vs AMP-3404 AC6a).

PART B

Calculation lab — the formulas behind the screens above

Interactive: change any input in the scenario panel and every figure below recomputes. Sections C1–C6 pair with the screens in Part A.
⚙

Scenario inputs (shared by every section)

These drive the whole page. The backend equivalent: application data + AECB report + product config.

Config knobs used below: exit-fee 1% (CBUAE cap) · absorption 100% · top-up cap 50% · DC buffer 1.05 · processing fee 1.05% (min 525 / max 2,625) · insurance 0.50% · Max DBR 50%.

C1

Settlement screen — what each contract "costs" per month (F5)

Before any limit can be calculated, every AECB contract is converted to a monthly obligation. This number sits behind the settlement cards and feeds the DBR.
Prototype: Your existing finances (buyout path)
F5 · Monthly obligation per contract — AMP-3732 AC4 Credit card / OD : MAX( cc% × CreditLimit , cc% × Balance ) Instalment loan : PaymentAmount (as reported by AECB)
  • Card: MAX(, )
  • Personal loan: PaymentAmount
  • Total monthly obligations

Why MAX(limit, balance)? A card can be drawn to its limit tomorrow — prudent banks reserve for the limit, not today's balance. When balance > limit (over-limit), the balance side wins.

C2

The hidden engine — DBR room → Max eligibility (F2 + F3)

No screen shows this directly, but it decides the ceiling of every slider. It answers: "how much monthly payment fits?", then "how big a loan can that payment carry?"
Inputs collected here feed this engine
F2 · DBR room — AMP-680 Room = MaxDBR% × Income − existing obligations
  • 50% ×
  • − obligations (from F5)
  • DBR room / month
F3 · Max eligibility = present value of the room — AMP-2239 MaxElig = Room × ( 1 − (1 + r/12)^(−N) ) / (r/12)
  • monthly rate r/12
  • (1 + r/12)^−N
  • annuity factor (1 − ·)/r12
  • Max eligibility (before product caps)
DBR usage today vs the 50% ceiling
current obligations ÷ income50% regulatory ceiling

Intuition: the annuity factor (~42.6 at 5.49%/48m) means "every 1 dirham of monthly room carries ~42.6 dirhams of loan". The bank then caps this at product max and decision boundary.

C3

Offer & Customise — the EMI itself (F1)

The number on the offer card. Every slider movement re-runs exactly this.
Prototype: You're approved for…
F1 · EMI (reducing balance) — AMP-11 EMI = P × (r/12) × (1 + r/12)^N / ( (1 + r/12)^N − 1 )
  • P (approved amount)
  • (1 + r/12)^N
  • EMI / month
  • Total payable = EMI × N
  • of which profit
Where the total payable goes
principalprofit

Amortisation — first 3 months and the last

#EMIProfitPrincipalBalance

Profit each month = balance × r/12; principal = EMI − profit. Early instalments are profit-heavy; that is why early settlement fees exist and why the KFS warns about longer tenors.

Engine check — prototype figures do not reconcile. The prototype offer shows 150,000 @ 5.49% / 48m with EMI 3,210 and total payable 250,000. F1 gives EMI 3,487.79 and total payable 167,414 (3,210 × 48 would be 154,080 — 250,000 is impossible at any of these numbers). The prototype's figures are illustrative; Hailey must bind every displayed number to the calculation service, never to screen copy.
C4

Buyout + Top-Up — the settlement arithmetic (F6 + F7)

What the bank pays the old bank, what the fee absorption costs, and how much cash is left for the customer.
Prototype: Ready to submit? (net breakdown)
F6 · Total buyout amount — AMP-3721 IA1 (+ CBUAE 1% exit cap) ExitFee = 1% × outstanding (capped by Reg. 29/2011) Absorbed = ExitFee × Absorption% Total = Settlement + Absorbed + Top-Up
  • Settlement (PL outstanding)
  • Exit fee 1%
  • Absorbed by bank
  • Committed to old bank
  • Top-up available = Approved − committed
  • F7 cap check: top-up ≤ % × approved =
How the approved amount splits
settlement to old bankabsorbed feetop-up cash to customer

If Settlement > Approved, top-up is negative — that is precisely the shortfall condition that triggers the DC fallback (next section). Try PL outstanding = 130,000 to see the cap-check verdict flip.

C5

Debt Consolidation — pool, new EMI, post-DBR, savings (F9 + F11)

The numbers behind the "Save AED X/mo" banner and gate G5. This is regulatory-grade benefit evidence — it must be exact.
Prototype: A buyout isn't possible → DC
F11 · DC new EMI & post-consolidation DBR — AMP-2328 / AMP-2329 Pool = Σ in-scope balances × 1.05 (5% settlement buffer) New EMI = PMT( MinRate/12 , Tenor , Pool ) ← same shape as F1 Post-DBR = ( New EMI + out-of-scope obligations ) / income → must be ≤ 50% (G5)
  • In-scope: PL + CC balance
  • × 1.05 buffer → pool
  • New EMI (one payment)
  • Post-consolidation DBR
Post-DBR vs gate G5 ceiling (50%)

Now → After → Save (the offer banner)

  • NOW: current PL EMI + card obligation
  • AFTER: one new EMI
  • SAVE per month

F9 auto-selection (shortfall case): rank contracts by cost-to-balance ratio, keep adding until Σ balances ≤ approved amount; loan = MAX(product min, Σ selected). The 1.05 buffer covers balance drift between AECB report date and actual settlement day.

C6

Insurance, fees & Net Amount Credited (F12 + F13)

The Review screen's waterfall — the last calculation the customer sees before signing.
Prototype: Protect your repayments
F12 + F13 — AMP-3404 AC8/AC9 Fee = clamp( fee% × Amount , min , max ) Insurance = ins% × Amount (or fixed AED) "Reduce from finance" Net = Amount − Fee − Insurance − Settlement
  • Approved / selected amount
  • − processing fee (clamped)
  • − insurance premium (year 1)
  • − settlement to old bank (incl. absorbed fee)
  • Net credited to customer
The waterfall
settlementfeeinsurancenet to customer

KFS check figures (F1-derived)

  • Total amount payable = EMI × N
  • Early settlement (month 12 example) = min(1.05% × balance, 10,500)

Fee caps (1.05% incl. VAT, min 525 / max 2,625; ES cap 10,500) mirror the prototype KFS and the market's "1% + VAT" pattern — still unverified against CBUAE Appendix 2 (open point).
